the_finding.headline: ⛔⛔ A REVIEW FINDING IS EVIDENCE WITH A DATE ON IT, AND THIS LIST HAD GONE STALE UNDER THE PAPER IT DESCRIBED. Of 16 P1s recorded against commit 34264bbeb610, ONE PAIR WAS THE SAME DEFECT (#1 and #13 both name §2.5's 'printed beside every pooled figure'), FOUR WERE ALREADY FIXED at the pinned commit (#2, #4, #12, #16), and TEN CARRIED A FACTUAL ERROR OF THEIR OWN — wrong counts, wrong sections, wrong direction, drifted line numbers. A cycle that had inherited this list as a summary would have re-applied fixes to text that no longer existed and re-litigated four closed findings, for the third cycle running.
the_finding.how_it_was_caught: The prompt that started this session deliberately carried no findings from its predecessor. The first live sentence read — the Abstract's '**Three** reports … **one** enters the primary pool' — is precisely what P1 #12 asserts is wrong, which is what turned round 4 from a review into a re-derivation.
the_finding.convergence: Seats A and D held disjoint slices, could not see each other, and landed on the SAME §2.5 defect from opposite directions — 'the declared substitute is not delivered' and 'the universality claim is false'. That decided the fix: PRINT the two missing per-cohort ranges (spread 53.9 pts and 22.4 pts, both wider than any range the paper did print) rather than soften the rule. A correction should deliver a paper's declared method, not retire it.
the_finding.one_claim_verified_TRUE: P1 #9 asserted the reader is asked to take an absolute author non-overlap claim on lists the synthesis cannot see the end of. The seat ran the check the finding said could not be run: all six pairwise intersections are empty, and complete lists for all four series were already committed on `main` in three artifacts nobody pointed the reader at. That reclassifies it from claim-integrity to provenance, at a materially lower weight than it was filed at — and the lists are now unabridged in the generator.
